replaces: week1/quality/results/schedule_restrictions.json (dev only; allowed everything because nothing was distinguishable at n = 250)
quality_gate: <= 5 pp accuracy loss vs static_L; pass only if the 95% paired bootstrap lower bound is >= -5 pp
task: GSM8K 8-shot CoT, base LM, greedy, exact match (week1/quality/manifests/quality_contract.json)
model: google/gemma-3n-E4B @ af70430f84ea4d7ac191aaa2bd8e14d2a5e8f6ee, bf16, NVIDIA L40S, batch 8

rules.decode_width: large for every generated token after the first
rules.switch_point: right after prefill (the first generated token comes from the small prefill pass)
rules.prefill_width: one width for the whole prompt; if prefill is chunked, every chunk of a request uses the same width
rules.per_iteration: one width per batch per iteration, so an iteration may run small only if every row in it is prefill; any iteration that carries a decode step runs large
rules.request_level: static large only; static small fails the gate

SL_early.meaning: small prefill, then large decode (the phase hybrid)

alt4.reason: fails on held-out and is significantly worse than large; stands in for all repeated switching

LS_early, LS_late, SL_late, alt16.reason: dev only, never run on held-out, so not certified; LS_* and alt16 also decode at small, which fails above

caveats: SL_early's +2.0 pp is noise in the favorable direction, not a gain: 99% of its steps run at large
batch noise floor: batch 1 vs batch 8 changed 4 of 48 static_L predictions (2 in correctness), so a few pp per-request variation comes from batching alone
one task (GSM8K) and one model; quality transfers to the serving harness only through the width history, not the prompts
block k = 1 alternation was not run; alt4 already fails, so it cannot change the rules
